comment: The table of the gate of the oracle test (test/fort/owner/oracle_test.ft), of the one
disposition table (test/fort/support/disposition.ft) and of the one judgement that gives
the gate each ruling (test/fort/support/judgement.ft). The gate fails an item when a run
gives an error event that no report line of its own rule takes on the line of the event
(D17.11, D17.20, D17.21). A row mutes one error kind in judgement.rule, or changes when a
`leak` or a `leak at exit` is an error. A change of `dk_error` to `dk_trusted` in the table
mutes no kind, because judgement.rule takes an event of a trusted kind as an error. Other
rows break the order of the table, change a count, a unit or a class of judgement.KNOWN,
or raise a row of FLOORS. Other rows give each item of one family an error, or take the
report lines of one option from each item. Other rows let a report line take an event of
another rule or of another line. No case of this test has a report line and an event of
another function on one line: the row judgement-report-each-function of
tools/mutations/generator.json holds that rule. One row takes each row of
FORCED from the case that only FORCED runs. The sources are test sources and no part of
the compiler binary. So the build writes the three into one file, and the md5 guard reads
that file. The stage runs the oracle test, which compiles the sources itself.
tools/mutations/generator.json holds the rows of the judgement that
test/fort/owner/typed/judgement_test.ft must catch.
A row counts as caught when the stage gives a FAIL line of test/lang/run_tests.py
(tools/mutate.py). The measurement ran on the named native host (arm64 Darwin, host build,
`--runner 'bash -c'`, with build/Linux/debug a link to the host build), not in the Linux VM.
